article.title: TotalView Debugger Adds Native Python Support for Parallel HPC Debugging
article.summary: Perforce's decades-old TotalView debugger, long limited to C/C++ and Fortran, now debugs Python in its latest release as the language spreads through HPC.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Perforce's TotalView, a parallel-application debugger built in the late 1980s for military use, now supports Python, the company said while demonstrating the tool at the SC26 supercomputing show this week, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). Until the latest quarterly release, TotalView had supported only C/C++ and Fortran, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564).

## What We Know

TotalView specializes in debugging applications that run in parallel across large numbers of processes, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). Perforce acquired the tool in 2019 as part of its purchase of Rogue Wave Software, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). Perforce's own version history lists the new Python capabilities under TotalView 2026.4, the most recent entry on its [what's-new page](https://www.perforce.com/products/totalview/whats-new), which the page says adds a launchable UI for single Python debugging sessions, configurable Python exception handling, and support for debugging worker processes created with Python's `multiprocessing.Process`, `multiprocessing.Pool`, and `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor`.

"In the HPC community, Python has grown in popularity," Bill Burns, Perforce's vice president of software engineering, told [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). The language's rise owes in part to the mpi4py library, which bridges Python programs to the Message Passing Interface so that parts of an application running on different hardware can communicate, [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564) reported. Python became more suited to parallel programming at the thread level with version 3.14, released a year earlier, which added concurrent interpreters and free-threading support by disabling the global interpreter lock, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). "If you have a CPU with 64 cores, you can run 64 independent threads all working in unison on that CPU. Without GIL, those threads will run fully asynchronously," Burns said, as reported by [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564).

That shift brings its own debugging headaches. "Now you're going to end up with lock and thread contention and race conditions and all the things that C++ and Fortran developers have dealt with for years," Burns said, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). TotalView is built to handle that scale: "Even if you have 10,000 things going on, if you have one crash in there, TotalView can pinpoint that," Burns said, able to inspect the state of a process, its threads, or the GPU it is using, [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564) reported.

Under the hood, TotalView uses Microsoft's debugpy engine, accessed through the Debug Adapter Protocol, to power a hierarchical tree server that aggregates hundreds of stack traces into a single view and flags only the ones outside expected bounds, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). A developer launches a single-process or parallel Python program under TotalView's control, then sets breakpoints, inspects variables and data structures, and evaluates expressions, [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564) reported. TotalView currently supports mpi4py and Python's built-in multiprocessing module out of the box; Perforce plans to add support for other concurrency frameworks, including Dask and PyTorch's torchrun, in future releases, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). The product is priced on a token-based model, where each token buys the capability to debug one process, [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564) reported.

## What We Don't Know

TotalView does not yet offer full cross-language debugging for Python applications that call into C/C++ libraries; developers currently have to choose between debugging the C/C++ side while viewing the Python stack, or debugging Python on its own, though Burns said Perforce plans to merge the two modes into a single workflow in a future release, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/11/17/python-parallel-debugging-comes-to-hpc-thanks-to-totalview-upgrade/5310564). Neither Perforce nor The Register's report gave a timeline for that merged workflow or for the planned Dask and torchrun support.
